summary: Embedding route affinity sync lag causes sudden 5xx elevation and runtime exit-loop during steady traffic
description:
Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-12 15:10 UTC, the embedding ingestion route serving Nimbus.ai started returning elevated 5xx rates from the API gateway. Errors escalated over ~20 minutes and coincided with repeated serving-runtime process exits on multiple hosts. Impact: Customer reports ~30% of embedding requests failing with 502/503/500; downstream batch ingest jobs retried and increased load. Environment: prod cluster in us-east serving dedicated Nimbus.ai tenant on dedicated GPU pool. Observed behavior: - API gateway returns ~10-30% 5xx for POST /v1/embeddings/bulk
- serving-runtime logs show short-lived process exits with SIGSEGV and watchdog restarts
- route-manager logs show a series of affinity sync messages delayed by 60-120s for the Nimbus route
Expected behavior: continuous low 5xx rate (<0.5%) and zero runtime exit-loop. Steps to reproduce (observed in prod): 1) Heavy concurrent small-batch embedding ingest from customer (500 concurrent small requests) 2) route-manager rollout triggered (partial control plane sync for affinity mapping) 3) within 30s, a burst of accepted connections hit runtimes with stale route-affinity entries 4) runtimes log connection handling errors, then exit-watchdog triggers restarts. Temporary mitigation performed: scaled down the concurrency from the customer side and rolled back the recent route-manager affinity rollout (see timeline).

comments: 2026-03-12 15:20 - Support (Aisha Khan): Customer reported increased 5xx on /v1/embeddings/bulk. They've paused new sends temporarily. Collected initial traces and asked SRE to triage.

2026-03-12 15:34 - SRE (Marco Delgado): Observed affinity-sync lag in route-manager; several runtimes crashed with SIGSEGV while handling prewarmed connections. Pinpointing which code path is dereferencing a freed connection struct.

2026-03-12 16:02 - Support (Aisha Khan): Rolled back route-manager rollout for tenant shard embed-12 as mitigation. 5xx rate decreased from ~22% to ~3% over 10 mins. Customer confirmed partial recovery.

2026-03-12 18:10 - Engineer (Priya Nambiar): Core suspect: race between affinity update path and runtime connection reaper. Preparing a small guard fix to check connection validity before use. Creating PR and will apply hotfix to canary pool.

2026-03-13 09:45 - SRE (Marco Delgado): Hotfix applied to canary (runtime binary v1.42.3-hotfix). No crashes observed in canary during equivalent synthetic workload. Scheduling rolling patch to remaining nodes after additional validation.

2026-03-14 07:12 - Support (Aisha Khan): Customer requested ETA for full patch and any permanent mitigations. Provided timeline and temporary config knobs (increase accept-queue, disable affinity-swap during high-concurrency windows).
investigation_notes: Affinity-sync path: route-manager sent delayed delta updates after a config sweep; affected runtimes still accepted prefetched connections referencing routes that had been freed.
Reproducer on staging: simulated delayed affinity apply + high connection churn reproduces crash in connection-handling.c: use-after-free of conn->route pointer when reaper runs concurrently.
Kernel / driver not implicated — SIGSEGV triggered deterministically from user-space pointer use after free in runtime code path that intersects with affinity update handler.
Canary hotfix (add null checks + refcount bump during affinity swap) prevents crash under synthetic load.
API gateway retry/hedging logic amplified load; hedged retries with overlapping windows increased concurrency against runtimes during affinity instability.
KV-cache warmup behavior: prefetching kept short-lived entries for stale routes which exacerbated connection handling complexity.
root_cause: Race condition in serving-runtime connection handling where a route-affinity update could free route metadata while an in-flight connection/reaper thread still referenced it, causing a use-after-free and SIGSEGV. This was amplified by delayed affinity-sync from route-manager and hedged retries at the API gateway increasing concurrent inflight connections.
resolution_notes: Immediate mitigation (2026-03-12 16:00): Rolled back route-manager affinity rollout for affected shard; asked customer to throttle concurrency briefly. Resulted in rapid reduction of 5xx.
Hotfix (2026-03-13 09:30): Deployed runtime binary v1.42.3-hotfix to canary with guard checks and temporary refcounting around route objects during affinity swap. Verified no crashes under load.
Full rollout (in progress 2026-03-14): Rolling patch to remaining prod runtimes with staged batch size 10 hosts, monitoring crash count and 5xx rate.
API gateway change: Short-term disabled hedged retries for embedding route for tenant Nimbus.ai to avoid amplification during rollout window.
Config tweak: increased accept-queue per runtime by 25% to reduce connection drop pressure during migration windows.
Postmortem prep: Drafting full RCA and runbook updates to route-affinity rollout procedure.

follow_up_actions: Merge runtime PR with guard and unit tests: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2421
Add metric: 'route_affinity_pending_ms' alert if >30s for any shard during active traffic
Update runbook: avoid affinity-rollout for dedicated tenants during known high-concurrency ingestion windows; add automated pre-checks
Create chaos test in CI that simulates delayed affinity propagation + high connection churn to catch regressions
Customer outreach: schedule post-incident sync with Nimbus.ai CS to review impacts and compensation per SLA
